messages.subject: Re: CODEX Troubleshooting - Discussion from ASHG
messages.body_plain:
Hi Kirsten,

Thanks again for your interest in CODEX. For LSU6q22, you cannot have a target that is 1bp long. See width(ref). They are all filtered out during the QC step — CODEX is for whole exome sequencing and targeted sequencing and filters out targets/exons that are small.

For the other, I cannot tell what is wrong from the rda file. What is the error message? Have you indexed the bam files or maybe renamed the bai files? This is due to something wrong at the first step, which is trivial and should be able to be fixed easily.

Yuchao

> On Nov 16, 2017, at 4:13 PM, Termine, Kirsten W. <kwo...@lsuhsc.edu> wrote:
>
> Hi Dr. Jiang,
>
> How are you?  My name is Kirsten Termine, and my mentor, Dr. Diptasri Mandal, and I spoke to you at your poster during ASHG last month regarding CODEX.  We spoke about the error messages we keep running into, and you asked us to send you the scripts, error messages and .rda files so that we could try to figure out what was going on. Attached are the scripts and .rda files (created using the command save.image(file ="CODEXdata.rda"), which includes the error messages generated, for two different datasets.
>
> One dataset is our prostate cancer whole-exome sequencing dataset, and the .rda file for this dataset is LSUPCaCODEXdata.rda and the script (for chromosome 1) is the file CODEXchr1.R.
>
> The second dataset is our lung cancer targeted dataset (6q22 region), and the .rda file for this dataset is LSU6q22CODEXdata.rda and the script is the file CODEXchr6.R.
>
> Each dataset has given us a different error message.
>
> We are hoping that with this information you will be able to help us figure out why we are running into the problems using CODEX so that we can fix the issue and successfully run CODEX on our datasets.  Please let me know if there is any additional information you need.
>
> Thank you for your time, and have a great day.
>
> Kirsten
>
> Kirsten Wood Termine, B.S.
> PhD Candidate in Dr. Mandal's Lab
> Department of Genetics
> Louisiana State University Health Sciences Center

Hi Yuchao,

Thank you so much for your quick response.  We greatly appreciate it.  So it seems that our LSU6q22 data, which was all generated using the same platform and therefore the same QC measures, will not be compatible with CODEX.  Is this correct?

Also, regarding the other dataset, here is the exact error we kept getting:

Error in .io_bam(.scan_bamfile, file, reverseComplement, yieldSize(file),  :

  seqlevels(param) not in BAM header:

    seqlevels: ‘9’

    file: s_4101_3.bam

    index: s_4101_3.bam

Calls: getcoverage ... scanBam -> scanBam -> scanBam -> scanBam -> .io_bam

Execution halted

The bam files are all indexed and named as a bam.bai extension of the sample.  For instance, for sample  s_4101_3, the bam for this sample is named s_4101_3.bam and the bai is s_4101_3.bam.bai.  All of the bam and bai files are located in the same directory.

Any ideas of what could be going on with this additional information?

Thank you again for your time.

Kirsten

Hi Kirsten,

For LSU6q22, I think it’s solved — you need to respecify your targets.

For the other, sorry I wish I could be of more help but like I said, this part of the code is from the dependent package to get the read depth from the bam files. I would suggest reassemble your bams using the same pipeline as the one you used for the samples that turned out to work. If the problem persists, you need to contact the developer for Rsamtools instead of us. Another way to go around is to generate the read count matrix R using samtools in Linux instead of Rsamtools, although I feel you may have the same issue.

Yuchao
